task_spec: subject: a deck-download-and-compare module for netrunneR's Sneakdoor Zeta ice/breaker app - fetch a Corp deck and a Runner deck from NetrunnerDB by ID/URL, then compute and display all ICE-vs-breaker pairings between the two decks

scope: ~/src/netrunneR on mediaServer (marcus@mediaServer), branch master - R/deck-compare.R (new), R/mod_matchup_explorer.R (extend, extract shared helper), R/fetch-nrdb.R (reuse nrdb_get()), inst/shiny-app/app_server.R and app_ui.R (wire the new view/modal)

out-of-scope: any new SQL table, any new lineage in .LINEAGE_REGISTRY, any persistence of fetched decks beyond one Shiny session, reconciliation against ABR, reprint/previous-versions schema work (flag as a follow-up gap, don't build it here)

out-of-scope for THIS session: pushing, committing-and-pushing, or opening a PR on netrunneR without asking first - standing instruction from earlier this session after an unrelated branch-cleanup overreach on this same repo. Planning and local implementation are fine; publishing is not, without explicit confirmation
constraints: MUST: no persistence - no dbWriteTable(), no SQL table, no store_root, no entry in .LINEAGE_REGISTRY, no fetch_lineage./build_lineage. methods for decks
MUST: deck card codes resolve in the SAME identity space as cardpool.sqlite's card.code column (5-digit NRDB codes) - verified these are identical, no translation layer
MUST: route deck-fetch HTTP through the existing nrdb_get() wrapper in R/fetch-nrdb.R (inherits NRDB_CONTACT header, req_throttle via pacing_rate, req_retry) rather than a second httr2 pipeline

MUST: validate the deck endpoint's response envelope as {success: bool, total: int, data: [...]} - checking success==TRUE, total==1, data present - this is a DIFFERENT envelope than the reviews/rulings endpoint's bare {data:[...]} shape netrunneR already calls; do not reuse compare_shape() as-is

MUST: an unresolved deck card code (not in the active cardpool release) does not abort the whole comparison - follow the codebase's existing degrade-and-label idiom (compute_ice_breaker_matchups()'s own not_computable / source column, fill_missing_columns()) rather than a hard abort; only refuse outright if a fetch returns zero identity/zero cards

MUST: distinguish two causes for an unresolved code rather than merging them into one generic error - (a) version skew: code is legitimately newer than the pinned/active cardpool release (not a bug in the deck), (b) reprint/unmapped: cardpool.sql has no previous-versions or reprint-alias column at all (confirmed by direct schema read) so this is a genuine gap to surface, not silently drop

MUST: reuse mod_matchup_explorer.R's existing filtering/render logic via a shared internal helper (parameterized by a code-set predicate) rather than duplicating a table component - matches the app's own established 'shared rendering lives once' convention (suite_nav_ui() is exported, one caller, not duplicated per view)

MUST: do not add a copy-count column to the matchup tibble - cost_to_break/credit_differential are per-card-title properties invariant to copy count; a copy-count badge belongs on the ICE group header, not threaded through shared matchup data

MUST: release-pinning transparency follows the EXISTING output$release_info caption convention (small muted caption, 11px, #8a8f98, styled inline not a new CSS class) added elsewhere in the app this same session - extend that caption, do not invent a new warning banner or modal

MUST: this repo enforces `make docs-current` (regenerated man/ and NAMESPACE must be committed alongside any roxygen @return/@export change) and `make test` (testthat, must stay FAIL 0) before anything lands - both verified working this session on a prior netrunneR commit (1001 passed, docs-current clean)

MUST NOT: rebuild anything resembling the deleted decklist-mirroring feature (decklist-sweep.R, an nrdb.sql decklist table, ABR-tombstone reconciliation) - R/README.md calls that 'a closed decision, not a gap to fill back in'. This module is a DIFFERENT shape (ephemeral fetch-compute-discard vs. a persisted/versioned lineage) and the user has confirmed that distinction, but the underlying three failure modes (wrong date field, fabricated identity_code, unserializable nested list-column into dbWriteTable()) must not recur even in the new, differently-scoped code
MUST NOT: push, commit-and-push, or open a PR against netrunneR without asking the user first - standing instruction, this session
entry_points: R/views-matchups.R:132-157 compute_ice_breaker_matchups(ice_breaker_traits, cardpool, matchup_overrides, cardpool_release_id, implementation_release_id) - already does a full cross-join of every ICE against every breaker in the WHOLE cardpool, joined on `code`. Returns a tibble with exactly: ice_code, breaker_code, cost_to_break, stealth_credits, credit_differential, source (source in formula/override/not_computable), arranged by ice_code, breaker_code. This is the ONLY shape available from it - no per-deck fields, by design (cardpool-wide, format-blind)

R/mod_matchup_explorer.R mod_matchup_explorer_server() - takes matchup + cards, filters all_pairs() down to a subject's rows, joins titles, optionally filters by legal_codes() from a format selector, sorts by cost_to_break, renders via reactable with columns [Counterpart, Cost to break, Credit differential, Source], em-dash for NA, whole-row-click opens card detail. Reached today as a modal from the card-detail modal. Its own doc comment explicitly killed an 'all vs all' third mode (21,377 rows, whole pool) as answering no real question - deck-compare is NOT that: two small named sets, tens of rows not thousands

R/fetch-nrdb.R nrdb_get() - httr2::req_user_agent(req, sprintf('netrunneR-mirror (%s)', contact)) with contact <- Sys.getenv('NRDB_CONTACT'), req_throttle() via pacing_rate(lineage$pacing), req_retry(max_tries=5). R/config.R's check_config() hard-aborts if NRDB_CONTACT is unset/placeholder

inst/sql/schema/cardpool.sql - card table has code TEXT PRIMARY KEY (5-digit NRDB code, verified against live data e.g. '00005'), no previous-versions/reprint-alias column anywhere (checked card, printing, card_set, restriction_card)

inst/shiny-app/app_server.R:176-186 (added this session) - output$nav renderUI(netrunneR::suite_nav_ui(view())); output$release_info renderUI(shiny::div(style='font-size: 11px; color: #8a8f98; padding: 2px 12px;', sprintf('cardpool %s · implementation %s', app_data$cardpool_release_id, app_data$implementation_release_id))) - the caption convention to extend for release-pinning transparency in the new view

R/operations.R load_ice_breaker_app_data() - builds app_data once per process (cardpool, implementation, matchup, cards, etc.); the Shiny app's single source of truth for the cross-join and the cardpool table the new module filters against

jinteki.net reference implementation (mtgred/netrunner, MIT licensed, already git-mirrored locally as netrunneR's own 'implementation' lineage): src/clj/web/nrdb.clj at /srv/netrunner-mirror/data/implementation/releases/a395d44c13fba31a46737336f94c0b483f9b1bb6-bad32763e17e7/raw/src/clj/web/nrdb.clj on mediaServer. Base URL https://netrunnerdb.com/api/2.0/public/, endpoints decklist/<id> (public) / deck/<id> (private). parse-input splits on 'decklist/|deck/view/|deck/', takes segment 2, splits again on '/' to strip trailing path. download-public-decklist guards nil-in/nil-out rather than throwing. lookup-card falls back to a previous-versions list on direct-code miss (netrunneR's schema has no equivalent - a confirmed gap, not a port target for v1)
rejected_alternatives: building a 6th mirrored lineage (deck as a persisted/versioned store_root entry) - rejected: exactly the shape of the deleted decklist-mirroring feature; decks are ephemeral per-comparison inputs, not a schedule-synced data source

reusing compare_shape() (the reviews/rulings envelope checker) for the deck endpoint - rejected: verified the deck endpoint's real envelope carries success/total fields the reviews/rulings endpoint's bare {data:[...]} shape does not; a weaker check would silently accept a malformed deck response

porting jinteki's Mongo previous-versions reprint fallback directly - rejected for v1: netrunneR's cardpool schema has no equivalent field, so a direct port would silently no-op; treat as a distinct, surfaced 'unrecognized code, possible reprint' case instead, and flag the schema gap to the cardpool lineage owner as a separate follow-up rather than patching around it inside this ephemeral module

abort-the-whole-comparison on any unresolved card - rejected: the codebase's actual established idiom (compute_ice_breaker_matchups()'s not_computable source, fill_missing_columns()) is degrade-and-label, not abort; matching that idiom is more consistent than inventing a new failure mode. NOTE: an earlier attempt to justify this via 'DL-008 abort-and-report, established elsewhere in the codebase' was WRONG - a sub-agent verified `grep -rn DL-008` returns nothing in netrunneR (DL-008 is a decision id from an unrelated project, traktor-nml-tool, mistakenly cross-referenced) - the degrade-and-label idiom is grounded in the REAL netrunneR pattern, not that false citation

a new copy-count column threaded through the shared matchup tibble - rejected: cost_to_break/credit_differential are per-card-title properties, invariant to how many copies are in a deck; a copy-count badge belongs on the UI's ICE group header, not in shared data both the single-card modal and deck-compare view read

a full ICE x breaker matrix/grid UI - considered, not chosen: defensible at deck-scale (roughly 8x5=40 cells) but reactable's existing row-based grouping already handles the 'grouped by ICE, expandable to breakers' shape natively, costing less than building a new grid component

a new standalone R/mod_deck_compare.R Shiny module mirroring mod_matchup_explorer.R's shape wholesale - INITIAL recommendation from one deepthink sub-agent (Architecture Placement), SUPERSEDED by a second sub-agent's (Comparison UX) better-grounded alternative: extract mod_matchup_explorer.R's filtering/render logic into a shared internal helper instead, since the app already has a real precedent for shared-not-duplicated chrome (suite_nav_ui()). The superseding position is what this plan should build against; a full duplicate module is the rejected path
current_understanding: netrunneR mirrors 5 lineages (nrdb, abr, cardpool, rules, implementation) with atomic release promotion via a store_root/releases/active-symlink pattern (lineage() in R/lineage.R, store_base() defaulting to /data unless NETRUNNER_STORE_BASE overridden)

The Shiny ice/breaker app (inst/shiny-app/) is design-driven: layout decisions are cited against specific wireframes in homelab/docs/netrunneR/design-references/wireframes/, and shared UI pieces (suite_nav_ui, matchup rendering) are kept as single exported functions rather than duplicated per caller

This session already added a live, working example of the exact caption convention the new feature should extend: app_server.R's output$release_info, merged and confirmed rendering correctly in a real browser session against the deployed app (homelab PR #18/#19, netrunneR PR #48, all merged)

Real scale check (queried directly against the active mirrored cardpool release, 69a34d7d...): 390 total ICE titles, 173 total icebreaker titles IN THE WHOLE CARD POOL. A single deck's unique-title counts are far smaller (single digits ICE, 3-6 breakers), so the deck-vs-deck cross-join is tens of rows, comfortably renderable, not a scale concern

This repo's release cadence is: source change -> make document (regenerate man/) -> make test -> make docs-current -> commit (including regenerated man/ in the SAME commit, per this repo's own docs-current gate) -> push/PR only with explicit confirmation given the standing instruction
assumptions: the operator-facing entry point is a new modal/panel reached from somewhere in the existing lane-board UI (mirroring how the single-card matchup explorer is reached from the card-detail modal) rather than a new top-level route - inferred from the app's own stated design convention of reaching secondary views from existing UI rather than adding navbar destinations the wireframes don't have (H)
two plain text inputs (Corp deck ID/URL, Runner deck ID/URL) plus a single 'Compare' button is sufficient v1 UI, no drag-drop or file upload needed, since NRDB deck sharing is URL/ID-based (H)

fetched deck state lives in ordinary Shiny reactiveVal()s scoped to one session, discarded on refresh/disconnect - no caching across sessions needed for v1 (M) - worth confirming since a popular deck could be fetched repeatedly; NRDB rate-limit/pacing headroom for this hasn't been measured under real interactive load, only inferred from the existing scheduled-sync pacing config

how common 'version skew' (a deck citing a card newer than the pinned cardpool release) will be in practice is unmeasured - reasoned about but not observed; may not need distinct UI treatment if actually rare (M, explicitly flagged as unresolved in the deepthink synthesis)
invisible_knowledge: DL-007-equivalent for netrunneR: this app's shared-rendering convention treats a component with no second caller yet (suite_nav_ui) as still exported/shared rather than folded inline, on the theory that a future caller shouldn't force extraction later - the same reasoning applies to extracting mod_matchup_explorer.R's filter/render logic now rather than after a second caller already exists

The decklist-mirroring deletion's three failure modes were ALL persistence-layer mistakes (wrong date field, fabricated identity_code, unserializable nested column into dbWriteTable()) - none of them are inherent to fetching or displaying deck data, only to STORING it as a versioned table. This is the load-bearing distinction that makes this feature not a violation of that closed decision, and should be stated explicitly in code comments/decision log so a future reader doesn't conflate the two the way the initial deepthink question itself did

netrunneR enforces its own docs-current gate in CI-adjacent tooling (make docs-current fails the build if man/ or NAMESPACE differ from what roxygen2 would generate from current R/ comments) - any exported function with an @export/@return needs man/ regenerated and committed in the same commit, never separately

The app's card-identity join key is always `code` (matching.py-equivalent convention throughout R/views-matchups.R, R/operations.R) - never title, never a synthesized id. Any new function resolving external data (a fetched deck) into this space must land on `code` or it silently produces zero matches rather than an error

This session already pushed a real production change through this exact release-pin cycle once (netrunneR#48 -> homelab pin bump -> image rebuild -> live browser verification) - that is the template for how a change here eventually reaches the deployed app, but is NOT to be repeated without the user's go-ahead given the standing confirm-first instruction
